entities.name: Stanisław of Skarbimierz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Stanisław of Skarbimierz (c. 1362–1431) stands as a pivotal figure in the intellectual and diplomatic landscape of late medieval Central Europe, primarily remembered as a jurist, theologian, and the inaugural rector of the re-established University of Krakow in 1399. Born in Skalbmierz, Poland, his career unfolded during a period of intense geopolitical and ecclesiastical upheaval, marked by the Western Schism and the persistent conflicts between the Kingdom of Poland and the Teutonic Knights. Stanisław's scholarly pursuits and diplomatic engagements were instrumental in shaping a distinct Polish school of international law, grounded in natural law principles, and in asserting Poland's sovereign rights on the European stage.

His tenure as rector (1399–1400, 1404–1405, 1411–1412) was critical to the institutional flourishing of the Krakow Academy, which, under his leadership, became a vibrant center for legal and theological studies. Stanisław authored significant works, most notably the *Sermones sapientiales*, a collection of 113 sermons that provided moral and legal guidance, and his seminal treatises on just war, delivered at the Council of Constance (1414–1418). Here, representing King Władysław II Jagiełło, he articulated a robust defense of the right of non-Christian peoples to self-governance and property, implicitly challenging the Teutonic Knights' aggressive crusading ideology and laying intellectual groundwork for religious tolerance.
